scope: Frozen candidate-facing and draft repair for phobias_nature; no source or runtime changes reviewed as approved.

blinding.limitation: The original quiz key was previously visible during the assigned original-source audit, so this is not a fully blind review. The frozen candidate-facing file was nevertheless solved before this draft/key comparison.

independent_candidate_answers.q_phobias_part_9_8: Человек пропускает дела из-за страха дождя

sources_opened.support: Defines acrophobia as intense fear of heights; gives balconies and distinguishes fear of flying from acrophobia.
Defines aerophobia as fear of airplane flying and lists takeoff, landing and turbulence as triggers.
Identifies thalassophobia as fear of large bodies of water and distinguishes aquaphobia as fear of water.
Dictionary entry gives acro- senses including height/top and identifies Greek akros as topmost/highest.
Defines ombrophobia as extreme fear of rain, including drizzle, and gives avoidance or skipped activities as examples.
Lists pyrophobia as fear of fire and distinguishes everyday strong fear from a phobia.
Defines astraphobia as fear of thunder and lightning and explicitly names brontophobia as another name.

items.key_compare: Candidate answer and draft key are Акрофобия.
items.evidence: Cleveland Clinic defines it as intense fear of heights and includes a balcony as an example.
items.distractors_and_explanation: The options name different objects or situations. The explanation accurately distinguishes the height object from fear of flying.

items.key_compare: Candidate answer and draft key are Аэрофобия.
items.evidence: Cleveland Clinic defines aerophobia as fear of flying in an airplane and supports the listed flight triggers.
items.distractors_and_explanation: The non-key options describe materially different fears. The explanation does not make a diagnostic claim.

items.key_compare: Candidate answer and draft key are Большими водоёмами.
items.evidence: Cleveland Clinic identifies thalassophobia as fear of large bodies of water, while aquaphobia concerns water more generally.
items.distractors_and_explanation: All distractors are outside that object. The specificity comparison in the explanation follows the source definitions.

items.key_compare: Candidate answer and draft key are Высота, верхушка.
items.evidence: Collins gives acro- senses including height, top and extremities, with Greek akros as topmost/highest.
items.distractors_and_explanation: The question asks for the applicable sense in акрофобия; the explanation preserves the broader dictionary nuance instead of treating acro- as only one sense.

items.key_compare: Candidate answer and draft key are Страх дождя.
items.evidence: Cleveland Clinic defines ombrophobia as extreme fear of rain, including a light drizzle.
items.distractors_and_explanation: The options name distinct weather phenomena. The explanation correctly avoids treating thunder or lightning as rain.

items.key_compare: Candidate answer and draft key are Высота над землёй.
items.evidence: Cleveland Clinic uses a balcony as a height example and specifically says fear of airplane flying may be aerophobia rather than acrophobia.
items.distractors_and_explanation: The scenario makes the height-versus-flying distinction without relying on the previously unsupported bathophobia/batheophobia synonym claim.

items.key_compare: Candidate answer and draft key are Пирофобия.
items.evidence: Cleveland Clinic lists pyrophobia as fear of fire and distinguishes ordinary strong fear from phobia.
items.distractors_and_explanation: All distractors have different objects. The explanation is appropriately framed as a general distinction, not an individual diagnosis.

items.key_compare: Candidate answer and draft key are Громом и молнией.
items.evidence: Cleveland Clinic defines astraphobia as fear of thunder and lightning and says brontophobia is another name for it.
items.distractors_and_explanation: The wording correctly tests the shared object of synonymous terms; it no longer offers the synonyms as competing answers.

items.key_compare: Candidate answer and draft key are Человек пропускает дела из-за страха дождя.
items.evidence: Cleveland Clinic lists skipping educational, professional or personal activities due to possible rain and notes impact on daily life.
items.distractors_and_explanation: The distractors are ordinary precautions; the keyed application is the only one showing avoidance with functional impact. It is a useful application item rather than the prior duplicate rain recall.

overall.risk: Educational terminology only. It must not be presented as a method to diagnose a person; the frozen draft itself makes no treatment recommendation.
